verdict: Amazon's sales rose 13% to $180.2B and AWS growth reached 20% — but $4.3B of one-off charges held operating income flat at $17.4B, while a $9.5B Anthropic gain lifted net income to $21.2B.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Stores, subscriptions and advertising in the US, Canada and Mexico; earned $4.8B of operating income — $7.3B before the FTC settlement charge.

segments.name: International
segments.note: Stores and subscriptions outside North America (+10% before currency effects); earned $1.2B of operating income.

segments.name: AWS
segments.note: Amazon Web Services cloud computing; earned $11.4B of operating income — two-thirds of Amazon's total, from 18% of its sales.

opex.name: Fulfillment
opex.note: Warehouses and delivery — getting orders to doors.

opex.name: Technology & infrastructure
opex.note: Engineers and the tech behind the store and AWS; up 30% YoY with the AI build-out.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Advertising Amazon's own services and sales teams.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Back-office costs: finance, legal and admin.

opex.name: Other operating expense, net
opex.note: Mostly this quarter's special charges: the $2.5B FTC legal settlement and $1.8B of severance for planned role eliminations.

otherDetail: Total non-operating income of $10,748M: a $9.5B pre-tax gain from revaluing Amazon's investment in Anthropic sits inside other income ($10,186M net), plus $1,100M of interest income less $538M of interest expense. Equity-method activity took off another $73M after tax.
follow100Note: The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: AWS growth picked up again
takeaways.text: AWS sales grew 20% to $33.0B and produced $11.4B of operating income — two-thirds of Amazon's total profit from 18% of its sales.

takeaways.title: One-off charges in the stores business
takeaways.text: Operating income includes a $2.5B legal settlement with the Federal Trade Commission and $1.8B of severance for planned role eliminations. Without them, operating income would have been $21.7B instead of a flat $17.4B.

takeaways.title: The AI build-out swallows the cash
takeaways.text: Free cash flow for the last twelve months fell to $14.8B, from $47.7B, because spending on property and equipment jumped $50.9B year over year — mostly AI. Operating cash flow still grew 16% to $130.7B.

oneTimers: Operating income includes two special charges totaling $4.3B: a $2.5B legal settlement with the Federal Trade Commission and $1.8B in estimated severance costs, primarily for planned role eliminations. Excluding these charges, operating income would have been $21.7B.
Net income includes a $9.5B pre-tax gain from the revaluation of Amazon's investment in Anthropic, recorded within other income.
